# APPROACH TO URINARY TRACT INFECTION (UTI)

# IDSA 2025 complicated and uncomplicated UTI definition updates:

Uncomplicated UTI is an infection confined to the bladder in afebrile women or

men without urinary catheter.

[Uncomplicated urinary tract infection](orzid3-gmenu-abx-uncomp-uti)

Complicated UTI is an infection beyond the bladder and accompanied by symptoms

including fever/other signs of systemic illness. Complicated UTI includes

pyelonephritis, febrile or bacteremic UTI, catheter-associated (CAUTI).

[Complicated UTI without catheter](orzid3-gmenu-abx-complicated-uti-no-catheter)

[Complicated UTI catheter associated](orzid3-gmenu-abx-complicated-uti-catheter-associated)

[Acute prostatitis](orzid3-gmenu-acute-bact-prostatitis)

For patients presenting with septic shock from a suspected urinary tract

infection: Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

Asymptomatic bacteriuria occurs in patients who have bacteria in the urine but

do not have symptoms of a urinary tract infection.

[Asymptomatic bacteriuria](orzid3-gmenu-asymp-bacteriuria)

Patients at risk of sexually transmitted infections should be assessed for

treatment:

[Sexually Transmitted Infections and HIV Exposure](orzid3-gmenu-sexually-transmitted-infections-sti)

Candida urinary tract infections are discussed elsewhere:

[Candida urinary tract infections](orzid3-gmenu-abx-candida-uti)
